brief.subject: Diesel falls 19.0 cents to $5.937; capacity keeps shrinking
brief.headline: Diesel Drops to $5.937 as Truckload Capacity Thins Despite Rate Recovery
brief.dek: Diesel fell 19.0 cents this week, carriers keep exiting despite stronger rates, and the Supreme Court reopens shipper liability questions.
brief.lede: Diesel fell 19.0 cents to $5.937 per gallon this week, a welcome break on the biggest variable cost for small carriers.

sections.heading: Diesel Slides Again
bullets: $5.937 per gallon is the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-11-16.
Down 19.0 cents (3.1%) from the prior week, easing per-mile costs heading into late November.
Down 33.9 cents over four weeks, a sustained drop worth checking against your fuel surcharge schedules.

sections.heading: Rates Up, Carriers Still Exiting
bullets: Truckload rates climbed much faster than costs in 2026, yet carrier failures continue, according to SONAR data.
Capacity is still declining as rates recover, a lag that could strengthen carrier leverage in 2027 contract bids.
Tender rejections are running at more than double last year's level, a sign shippers are struggling to cover freight.

sections.heading: Shipper Liability Back in Play
bullets: The U.S. Supreme Court sent Casarez vs. Irigoyen Farms back to a lower court on Monday via grant, vacate, remand.
The move could set up a major ruling on whether shippers and receivers share liability after Montgomery.
Outcome could shape how shippers vet and select carriers, including smaller operators.

sections.heading: Enforcement Blitzes Sideline Trucks
bullets: Over 284 out-of-service violations turned up in recent enforcement operations across the U.S. and Canada.
More than 76 drivers and 208 trucks were placed out of service, a reminder to tighten pre-trip checks and paperwork.

sections.heading: Big Players Signal Cost Relief
bullets: J.B. Hunt told investors cost pressures are easing and it is winning new dedicated business.
J.B. Hunt said BNSF's rail outage had minimal impact on its volumes.
Amazon's 3.5% fuel and logistics surcharge expands to bulk storage and replenishment transportation fees starting in February.
